records.excerpt: Skip to main content Accessibility help AI Mode All Forums Videos Images Shopping Short videos More Tools Search Results AI Overview To access church and baptismal records for genealogy in San Diego, you must use the The Roman Catholic Diocese of San Diego for modern Catholic records, or the FamilySearch Catalog for microfilmed historical mission registries. 1. Roman Catholic Diocese Archives The majority of sacramental records (baptisms, marriages, burials) in San Diego remain privately held by the Catholic Church. Modern and Parish Records: Sacramental records are strictly not open to public examination. To request a record, you must be the individual on the record or a verifiable family member. How to Request: You can submit an inquiry by completing the Request an Archive form on the official The Roman Catholic Diocese of San Diego website. 2. FamilySearch Historical & Mission Records For early Californian history and 19th-century ancestors, extensive parish and mission logs have been digitized and microfilmed. Mission San Diego de Alcala: The registry books dating back to 1771 are cataloged. You can explore transcribed and translated volumes such as the Book of baptisms, San Diego Mission. Parish Microfilms: General historical parish records spanning 1771–1904 are available for digital review in the Parish records (San Diego, Calif.), 1771-1904 collection. 3. Local In-Person Research San Diego FamilySearch Center: You can visit the local Welcome to the San Diego, California FamilySearch Center. The center provides free access to premium genealogy partner sites (like Ancestry.com and MyHeritage) and allows you to view restricted microfilms that are only available within the building. San Diego History Center: The San Diego History Center archives hold significant genealogical indices and collections (such as the San Diego Genealogical Society Collection), which often index early church events and pioneers. Further Exploration Learn more about the specific jurisdictions and available regional collections via the San Diego County, California Genealogy wiki page. Check additional digitized Catholic church films in the comprehensive California Church Records overview. Many of the records published in the San Diego Leaves and Saplings issues are listed below by category with their corresponding volume and number. You can review the full Surname index of each volume at Indexes - Leaves & Samplings. As a member of SDGS you can read the full volumes of San Diego Leaves and Saplings in the Members Only section. Non-members can research San Diego Leaves and Saplings in libraries, archives and genealogical collections across the United States. Locally in San Diego County they can be found at the local library downtown and at the Carlsbad Library. They are also indexed in the Allen County Public Library's PERSI (PERiodical Source Index).
